newsitem.title: UK: London stocks start 1997 on a sour note.
newsitem.headline: London stocks start 1997 on a sour note.

text.p: UK shares suffered a dismal start to the New Year on Thursday, ending sharply lower after fresh U.S. economic data strengthened fears of inflationary pressures and spooked financial markets.

London's FTSE 100 index of leading shares lost 61.1 points, or 1.5 percent to close at 4,057.4, after U.S. bond and stock markets reacted violently to signs of stronger than expected manufacturing activity.

Trade remained subdued, however, with many investors taking extended New Year holidays. Dealers said slim volumes had exaggerated share price movements. Losses were broadly based, with only a handful of stocks managing to stay in positive territory.
The Mid-250 index fared better though, shedding just 0.47 percent or 21 points to 4,469.4.
The UK stock market got off to a poor start in the morning in response to sharp losses in the U.S. on Tuesday, after the London markets had already closed for the New Year holiday.

After clawing back the bulk of initial losses to reach a day's best of 4,095.3, the FTSE turned lower once again when Wall Street was surprised by fresh evidence that the U.S. economy was growing strongly.
